machine: Apple M5, Chrome, ANGLE Metal, 120 Hz display, DPR 2, on battery (97-98%, rAF 122 Hz, not throttled)
preset: Balanced (pixel ratio 1.25, 60 FPS cap, 3 bloom levels; saved settings unchanged)
baseline: 4.2 (f8d3b19) served from a git worktree on port 5174 in the same browser tab, runs alternated with 5.0 on port 5173

aiBench.method: __dev.aiBench(): Arcade, god mode, wave 6 (10 alive), the player at the level start shooting at the nearest enemy every 0.6 s; 14 s settle, 5 s measured. aiMs = wall time inside Waves.update (director + decides + every enemy act); rays = collision raycasts made inside it. Each version: page reload, two rounds back to back; both rounds listed.

4.2_first_measurement.note: the very first baseline run of the session (same bench, before any 5.0 code existed)

dev_bench.method: __dev.bench(3) per setting (Tokyo in Story mode with no guards; desert and jungle in Arcade, their 'fight' scenarios with waves). Page opened with ?setting=tokyo for both versions (same load order). All measurements valid (focused, visible, in play).
dev_bench.caveat: Earlier in the session several 5.0 runs measured 4.7-6.2 ms CPU per frame in Tokyo for 15-25 s after a page load, uniformly slower in code 5.0 did not change (story rules 0.7-0.85 vs 0.45 ms). It did not depend on the AI (freezing Waves.update and hiding every enemy left it unchanged) and did not reproduce on later loads of the same build (2.6-2.8 ms). Recorded as a machine-state effect (on battery), not attributed to 5.0; the table above is a later, alternated pair.

ai_cost_breakdown_desert.method: wall time per frame, 10 enemies, wave 6, after the steering cache
